display: Graham Tulloch, one-man timber mill outside Castlemaine, central Victoria: quartersawing, resawing, de-nailing and solar kiln drying of Victorian hardwoods and salvaged oregon and old-growth pine. 26 years in the trade.

signals.text: I'd like to find new customers for kiln drying, custom quartersawing and de-nailing, because my usual word-of-mouth has dried up.
I'm looking for people who work in Victorian hardwoods (blackwood, ash, box, stringybark) and need a reliable local supplier.
The kiln and resaw are mostly idle at the moment, and I could turn around a kiln charge or a resaw job quickly.

I'm holding a half-charge of kiln-dried quartersawn blackwood and two stacks of Victorian ash that need a buyer, and I'd rather sell them to someone who'll use them well than discount them for a stranger.
I supplied one furniture maker for eleven years and he took most of my kiln output. He has retired, and I'm now learning what it costs to have all my eggs in one basket.
I want a second and third regular customer, so I'm not dependent on a single buyer again.
I keep running the kiln a few days a fortnight just to keep it warm, and it's hard to see that going on much longer without paying work.
My income is well down since mid-year, and big overheads (roof, insurance, truck repairs) are landing at the same time.
I'm after jobs I can do within about two hours' drive: doors, benchtops, mantels, flooring and restoration timber.
I'd like to get hold of large-section old-growth or demolition timber, and I'd mill it properly, nails and wire included.
I'm cutting and planing species samples for the Castlemaine Historical Society display, which opens 21 October, and I'd enjoy talking with anyone who knows local timber history.
I'm clearing fire-prep jobs around the shed before the November fire season, and I'm short on hands for tree trimming.
I'm learning Italian for a trip next September (Piedmont, then Cremona to see the violin makers), and I'd happily swap practice with a native speaker.
I work alone most days and a visitor to the shed, a bit of conversation or a joint project would be welcome.

offers.text: Quartersawing and rift-cutting on a Wood-Mizer LT40 bandsaw mill and a 24-inch resaw bandsaw, both sharpened in-house, mostly Victorian hardwoods.
Solar kiln drying, about 6 cubic metres per charge, taking green boards to 10-12 percent moisture in 8-12 weeks depending on species. Large runs need a month's notice.
De-nailing and de-fixing salvaged beams and demolition timber, using a metal detector wand and nail pullers to find old fixings before the blade touches the wood.
Access to occasional salvaged oregon and old-growth pine, plus 26 years of knowledge about which species and cuts suit furniture, joinery and restoration.
Six acres with a workshop, concrete slab and yard holding about 40 cubic metres of stacked stock, plus a forklift, tipper trailer and a tray truck for pickups and deliveries within about two hours.
Cutting and planing labelled timber cross-sections and species samples for museums, schools and displays (seventeen local species done so far).
Kiln-dried quartersawn blackwood and Victorian ash in stock, and I know them well enough to advise on grain, movement and finishing.
Local knowledge of central Victoria's hardwood species, old sawmills and demolition sources, built from years volunteering with the historical society.

catchers.hypo: I'm a furniture maker in central Victoria and my usual kiln-dried hardwood supplier has closed. Do you know anyone who can supply dried quartersawn blackwood or Victorian ash in table-sized quantities?
catchers.can: Graham has dried quartersawn blackwood and ash on hand and spare kiln capacity, and he can supply or dry to order. He also knows the retired furniture maker who used to take most of his output and may know other makers.
catchers.confirm: Do you need Victorian-grown hardwood that has been kiln-dried to about 10-12 percent for indoor furniture?

catchers.hypo: I'm a luthier or guitar/ukulele maker looking for quartersawn Australian blackwood tonewood that is well dried and sized for sets.
catchers.can: Graham can quartersaw and kiln-dry blackwood to a stable moisture content and cut billets to a requested thickness. He is also curious about the tonewood trade, because he plans to visit Cremona.
catchers.confirm: Are you looking for hobby-to-small-workshop quantities of blackwood rather than guaranteed instrument-grade sets?

catchers.hypo: We're a local museum, historical society or school building a display of regional timber species and need cross-sections, dated samples or plank offcuts cut and planed.
catchers.can: Graham is already doing this for the Castlemaine Historical Society and can cut, plane and label samples. Dorothy, the society's secretary, knows the local history side and can link you to the society.
catchers.confirm: Is your display about timbers from central Victoria or species that Graham can cut from logs or stock?

catchers.hypo: I'm renovating or rebuilding a heritage house and have old beams or floorboards with nails and wire still in them. Can anyone de-nail and resaw them safely into usable boards?
catchers.can: Graham scans each beam with a metal detector, de-nails by hand and resaws on the bandsaw, and he can kiln-dry the result. He won't take lead-painted or treated timber.
catchers.confirm: Is the timber untreated and free of lead paint, and within about two hours' drive of Castlemaine?

catchers.hypo: We're a boatbuilder or small workshop on the Surf Coast and need well-seasoned local hardwood or salvaged oregon, and we're open to buying from a sawmill inland.
catchers.can: Graham's sister is a nurse in Torquay and could pass the word along locally, though the drive is near his two-hour limit. He would likely do pickup or delivery in bulk.
catchers.confirm: Could you accept a delivery run of at least a few cubic metres, rather than a single plank?

catchers.hypo: I'm a retired woodworker in the district with a shed full of timber I can't use any more. Do you know anyone who would buy or mill it?
catchers.can: Graham could look at the stock, de-nail and mill it, or help the owner find a buyer. He understands that moment, having just watched a long-time customer retire.
catchers.confirm: Is the timber stacked and accessible to a truck within about two hours of Castlemaine?

catchers.hypo: My neighbour and I each need a door made from quartersawn oak, and we'd like a mill that can supply flat, stable boards for a door-sized opening.
catchers.can: Graham is already doing a rift-cut oak door for a Daylesford customer and can quote more doors from photos of the opening.
catchers.confirm: Can you send photos and measurements of the opening, and is the job within about two hours of Castlemaine?

catchers.hypo: I run a small furniture or cabinet shop and want a regular supplier who can hold stock, kiln-dry on a schedule and deliver every few weeks.
catchers.can: Graham has spare kiln capacity and wants to build two or three standing arrangements. He could hold stock for you and run charges on a fixed rhythm with a month's notice.
catchers.confirm: Would you order on a regular rhythm, with kiln runs planned about a month ahead?

catchers.hypo: I'm a native Italian speaker or Italy traveller based in central Victoria, and I'd be glad to chat over coffee with a learner who is planning a trip to Piedmont and Cremona.
catchers.can: Graham is nineteen lessons into Italian and wants conversation practice, and he'd swap it for a tour of the mill.
catchers.confirm: Are you happy to speak slowly and put up with a beginner who still sounds like a tourist?

forbids.text: Won't mill treated pine or anything with lead paint.
Won't take jobs needing heavy highway driving of more than two hours each way.
No weekend work, except fire-prep on his own property.
Large kiln runs need at least a month's notice.
Won't undercut his own prices to a point where the work loses money.

projects.name: Kiln and resaw capacity
projects.text: Rebuilding a customer base for a solar kiln and resaw mill after the main long-term customer retired: kiln-dried Victorian hardwoods, quartersawing, de-nailing, with standing arrangements preferred.

projects.name: Historical society timber display
projects.text: A display of local timber species with dated cross-sections for the Castlemaine Historical Society, opening 21 October, with seventeen species cut so far.
roles_needed: people with old sawmill photos or records

policy.t1: Once there is a real prospect, he will share that the kiln and resaw are mostly idle, rough capacity and turnaround times, what stock he's holding, and who his past customers were.
policy.t2: Once the match looks strong and the other party is clear, he will share that his main customer retired, that income has dropped, and that cash is tight, and he'll mention health or physical limits where they affect the work.
policy.never: Bank, overdraft and other money figures, family disagreements, and personal details about his sister.
